## 1. Introduction

This report examines the construct validity and internal consistency of two four-item scales in Case 31: **R3, attitude toward employee proficiency (Q3–Q6)**, and **R6, attitude toward operational effectiveness (Q31–Q34)**. Separate exploratory factor analyses examine convergent validity; a joint two-factor analysis provides evidence about discriminant validity. Cronbach's alpha assesses internal consistency. These analyses inform whether to create composite scores for subsequent research; they do **not** test substantive R3 or R6 research hypotheses.

## 2. Data preparation

Place `Case31_cleaned.sav` in the **same folder** as this QMD file. Install packages once if necessary: `install.packages(c("haven", "psych", "knitr"))`.

```{r}
library(haven)
library(psych)
library(knitr)

file_path <- "Case31_cleaned.sav"
if (!file.exists(file_path)) stop("Put Case31_cleaned.sav in the same folder as this QMD file.")
dat <- read_sav(file_path)
names(dat) <- tolower(names(dat))
r3_vars <- paste0("q", 3:6)
r6_vars <- paste0("q", 31:34)
all_vars <- c(r3_vars, r6_vars)
if (!all(all_vars %in% names(dat))) stop("Missing variables: ", paste(setdiff(all_vars, names(dat)), collapse = ", "))

# Convert labelled SPSS survey responses to numeric without changing their codes.
items <- as.data.frame(lapply(dat[all_vars], function(x) as.numeric(x)))
# Use a common complete-case sample for comparable factor analyses.
items <- items[complete.cases(items), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(items) < 10) stop("Too few complete observations for the analysis.")
if (any(vapply(items, sd, numeric(1)) == 0)) stop("At least one item has no variance.")
r3 <- items[r3_vars]
r6 <- items[r6_vars]

item_labels <- c(
  q3 = "Employees are courteous", q4 = "Employees are helpful",
  q5 = "Employees are professional", q6 = "Employees are available",
  q31 = "CU confidential", q32 = "CU is prompt",
  q33 = "CU meets members' needs", q34 = "CU loan applications simple"
)
kable(data.frame(Item = all_vars, Description = unname(item_labels[all_vars]),
                 Missing_in_analysis = colSums(is.na(items[all_vars]))),
      caption = "Items included in the complete-case analysis")
cat("Complete-case sample size:", nrow(items), "\n")
```

**Coding check:** The analysis uses the numeric values stored in the cleaned SPSS file. Before interpreting or averaging items, confirm that higher responses consistently represent more favorable attitudes; reverse-code any oppositely worded items if necessary. This report does not assume an undocumented reverse-coding scheme.

## 3. Convergent validity: separate factor analyses

A coherent one-factor solution with substantial item loadings and communalities supports convergent validity. For classroom interpretation, loadings of approximately **0.50 or higher** and communalities of approximately **0.40 or higher** are useful guidelines, not universal cutoffs. We use minimum-residual exploratory factor analysis on Pearson correlations. Eigenvalues and parallel analysis can help assess the number of factors; a forced one-factor solution alone does not establish unidimensionality.

```{r}
# Parallel analysis uses the observed data to help assess factor retention.
set.seed(31)
pa_r3 <- fa.parallel(r3, fa = "fa", fm = "minres", plot = FALSE, n.iter = 100)
pa_r6 <- fa.parallel(r6, fa = "fa", fm = "minres", plot = FALSE, n.iter = 100)
fit_r3 <- fa(r3, nfactors = 1, fm = "minres", rotate = "none")
fit_r6 <- fa(r6, nfactors = 1, fm = "minres", rotate = "none")

factor_table <- function(fit, vars) {
  data.frame(Item = vars,
             Loading = round(as.numeric(fit$loadings[, 1]), 3),
             Communality = round(as.numeric(fit$communality), 3),
             Uniqueness = round(as.numeric(fit$uniquenesses), 3))
}
r3_table <- factor_table(fit_r3, r3_vars)
r6_table <- factor_table(fit_r6, r6_vars)
```

### 3.1 R3: Attitude toward employee proficiency (Q3–Q6)

```{r}
kable(r3_table, caption = "R3 one-factor loadings and communalities")
cat("Parallel analysis suggested", pa_r3$nfact, "factor(s) for R3.\n")
cat("Variance explained by one-factor solution:",
    round(100 * fit_r3$Vaccounted[2, 1], 1), "%\n")
```

**Interpretation.** Parallel analysis suggested **`r pa_r3$nfact` factor(s)** for R3. The one-factor model accounts for **`r round(100 * fit_r3$Vaccounted[2, 1], 1)`%** of standardized item variance. The smallest absolute factor loading is **`r round(min(abs(r3_table$Loading)), 3)`** and the smallest communality is **`r round(min(r3_table$Communality), 3)`**. `r if (pa_r3$nfact == 1 && all(abs(r3_table$Loading) >= .5) && all(r3_table$Communality >= .4)) "Together, these results support a coherent single-factor interpretation and provide evidence of convergent validity." else "These results do not fully satisfy the illustrative one-factor/loading/communality criteria; inspect the item-level results before claiming convergent validity."`

### 3.2 R6: Attitude toward operational effectiveness (Q31–Q34)

```{r}
kable(r6_table, caption = "R6 one-factor loadings and communalities")
cat("Parallel analysis suggested", pa_r6$nfact, "factor(s) for R6.\n")
cat("Variance explained by one-factor solution:",
    round(100 * fit_r6$Vaccounted[2, 1], 1), "%\n")
```

**Interpretation.** Parallel analysis suggested **`r pa_r6$nfact` factor(s)** for R6. The one-factor model accounts for **`r round(100 * fit_r6$Vaccounted[2, 1], 1)`%** of standardized item variance. The smallest absolute loading is **`r round(min(abs(r6_table$Loading)), 3)`** and the smallest communality is **`r round(min(r6_table$Communality), 3)`**. `r if (pa_r6$nfact == 1 && all(abs(r6_table$Loading) >= .5) && all(r6_table$Communality >= .4)) "The pattern supports convergent validity for a single operational-effectiveness construct." else "The pattern requires caution: some evidence is inconsistent with the illustrative criteria for a single coherent factor."`

## 4. Discriminant validity: joint factor analysis

To investigate whether the two constructs are distinguishable, all eight items are analyzed together using a **two-factor** minimum-residual model with oblimin rotation. The expected pattern is that Q3–Q6 load mainly on one factor, while Q31–Q34 load mainly on the other. Because oblimin permits correlated factors, factor correlation is also reported. This is exploratory evidence, not definitive proof of discriminant validity.

```{r}
set.seed(31)
pa_all <- fa.parallel(items, fa = "fa", fm = "minres", plot = FALSE, n.iter = 100)
fit_joint <- fa(items, nfactors = 2, fm = "minres", rotate = "oblimin")
joint_load <- as.matrix(fit_joint$loadings)
joint_table <- data.frame(Item = rownames(joint_load),
                          round(joint_load[, 1:2, drop = FALSE], 3),
                          Communality = round(fit_joint$communality, 3),
                          check.names = FALSE)
kable(joint_table, caption = "Joint exploratory factor analysis: rotated pattern matrix")
cat("Parallel analysis suggested", pa_all$nfact, "factor(s) across eight items.\n")
cat("Factor correlation matrix:\n")
print(round(fit_joint$Phi, 3))
```

```{r}
# Check whether each group has a different dominant factor.
major <- apply(abs(joint_load), 1, which.max)
separated <- length(unique(major[r3_vars])) == 1 &&
  length(unique(major[r6_vars])) == 1 &&
  major[r3_vars][1] != major[r6_vars][1]
# Dominant loading should also be reasonably substantial and clearly higher.
primary <- apply(abs(joint_load), 1, max)
secondary <- apply(abs(joint_load), 1, min)
clean_pattern <- separated && all(primary >= .5) && all(primary - secondary >= .2)
```

**Interpretation.** Parallel analysis suggested **`r pa_all$nfact` factor(s)** across all eight items. `r if (clean_pattern) "The rotated loading matrix shows the anticipated separation of the R3 and R6 items, with primary loadings of at least 0.50 and differences from secondary loadings of at least 0.20. This supports discriminant validity." else "The rotated matrix does not meet all of the illustrative simple-structure criteria. Examine the loadings, cross-loadings, and factor correlation carefully before asserting discriminant validity."` The estimated correlation between the two factors is **`r round(fit_joint$Phi[1,2], 3)`**. Strong factor correlation would warrant additional caution even if the items load on separate factors.

## 5. Reliability: Cronbach's alpha

Cronbach's alpha assesses internal consistency. As a common classroom benchmark, **α ≥ 0.70** suggests acceptable internal consistency, but alpha alone does not establish validity or unidimensionality. Item-total correlations and alpha-if-item-deleted are useful diagnostic checks.

```{r}
a_r3 <- psych::alpha(r3, check.keys = FALSE)
a_r6 <- psych::alpha(r6, check.keys = FALSE)
reliability_summary <- data.frame(
  Scale = c("R3: Employee proficiency", "R6: Operational effectiveness"),
  N_items = c(ncol(r3), ncol(r6)),
  Cronbach_alpha = round(c(a_r3$total$raw_alpha, a_r6$total$raw_alpha), 3),
  Standardized_alpha = round(c(a_r3$total$std.alpha, a_r6$total$std.alpha), 3)
)
kable(reliability_summary, caption = "Internal consistency of R3 and R6")
cat("R3 item diagnostics:\n")
print(round(a_r3$item.stats[, c("r.drop"), drop = FALSE], 3))
print(round(a_r3$alpha.drop[, c("raw_alpha"), drop = FALSE], 3))
cat("R6 item diagnostics:\n")
print(round(a_r6$item.stats[, c("r.drop"), drop = FALSE], 3))
print(round(a_r6$alpha.drop[, c("raw_alpha"), drop = FALSE], 3))
```

### 5.1 R3 reliability interpretation

R3 has a Cronbach's alpha of **`r round(a_r3$total$raw_alpha, 3)`**. `r if (a_r3$total$raw_alpha >= .7) "This meets the commonly used 0.70 benchmark for acceptable internal consistency." else "This falls below the commonly used 0.70 benchmark, so internal consistency is questionable and individual items should be examined."`

### 5.2 R6 reliability interpretation

R6 has a Cronbach's alpha of **`r round(a_r6$total$raw_alpha, 3)`**. `r if (a_r6$total$raw_alpha >= .7) "This meets the commonly used 0.70 benchmark for acceptable internal consistency." else "This falls below the commonly used 0.70 benchmark, so internal consistency is questionable and individual items should be examined."`

## 6. Implications for future analysis: composite scales

A composite mean score should be considered only if the item coding is consistent, the intended scale is substantively meaningful, the factor evidence supports the proposed structure, and reliability is adequate. The following decisions use transparent **illustrative** screening criteria; they are not universal statistical rules.

```{r}
r3_ok <- pa_r3$nfact == 1 && all(abs(r3_table$Loading) >= .5) &&
  all(r3_table$Communality >= .4) && a_r3$total$raw_alpha >= .7
r6_ok <- pa_r6$nfact == 1 && all(abs(r6_table$Loading) >= .5) &&
  all(r6_table$Communality >= .4) && a_r6$total$raw_alpha >= .7
recommendation <- data.frame(
  Scale = c("R3", "R6"),
  Convergent_screen = c(r3_ok && pa_r3$nfact == 1, r6_ok && pa_r6$nfact == 1),
  Reliability_alpha = round(c(a_r3$total$raw_alpha, a_r6$total$raw_alpha), 3),
  Joint_two_factor_pattern = rep(clean_pattern, 2),
  Recommendation = c(if (r3_ok && clean_pattern) "Consider composite after coding check" else "Review before combining",
                     if (r6_ok && clean_pattern) "Consider composite after coding check" else "Review before combining")
)
kable(recommendation, caption = "Screening summary for potential composite scores")
```

**R3 decision:** `r if (r3_ok && clean_pattern) "The results support considering a mean composite for Q3–Q6, provided the response directions have been verified." else "Do not automatically combine Q3–Q6 into a single composite; review the factor structure, individual items, and response coding first."`

**R6 decision:** `r if (r6_ok && clean_pattern) "The results support considering a mean composite for Q31–Q34, provided the response directions have been verified." else "Do not automatically combine Q31–Q34 into a single composite; review the factor structure, individual items, and response coding first."`

If supported, possible future score definitions are `rowMeans(r3, na.rm = FALSE)` and `rowMeans(r6, na.rm = FALSE)` after checking coding. **No composite variables are created in the dataset as part of this assignment.** The substantive R3 and R6 research questions will be addressed in a later activity.

## 7. Conclusion

The separate factor analyses, joint two-factor analysis, and Cronbach's alpha provide complementary evidence about the proposed scales. Factor structure and item communalities inform convergent validity; separation of the two item groups informs discriminant validity; and Cronbach's alpha informs internal consistency. Composite scores should be adopted only when the total pattern of evidence and item coding justify doing so.
